content:
I first saw the Ohsnap MCON controller at CES last year and was immediately drawn to the concept. The idea is simple: a fully featured portable controller that attaches to your phone via MagSafe, slides out when you need it, and folds away when you don't, so you can take it anywhere. For the past two weeks, I put it through a comprehensive test, playing with it constantly, pressing the launch button hundreds of times, and using it with emulators, Apple Arcade games, and multiple phones. Here's how it actually performs, and everything you need to know.

Be sure to check out my video as well to see it in action!

At first glance, the MCON looks like a large MagSafe battery pack. On the front is an adjustable magnetic mount for your phone, with all the buttons, sticks, and grips tucked away behind it. Some key specs include:

  • Full-size GameSir Mag-Res TMR joysticks
  • Hall effect analog triggers
  • Buttons include: ABXY buttons, D-pad, LB/RB bumpers, Start, Select, and Home buttons
  • Modular design with kickstand support
  • Up to 9 hours of battery life on a single charge
  • Bluetooth 5.4 and USB-C connectivity
  • Only 197 grams

On paper, the specs look like those of a standard controller that checks all the boxes, but what really impresses is the actual hardware build. The centerpiece of the design is the Launch button. Press it and the phone slides up, revealing all the controls. The grips on the back then flip out and lock into place, turning the MCON into the shape of a traditional controller, which feels much better in the hand. I've used this sliding mechanism countless times, and the build quality is exceptionally solid. Even with heavier phones like the 17 Pro Max or the unfolded Fold 7, the sliding mechanism handles the weight with ease.

Kickback Mode

But that's not all this design offers. There's a second way to use it, called Kickback Mode. You can remove the metal MagSafe baseplate from the bottom, which also houses a built-in kickstand. You can then place your phone on a table, prop it up with the stand, and connect the controller wirelessly to play, giving you a Switch-like handheld gaming experience. If you find holding the entire controller with your phone attached too heavy, you can simply detach the phone and play in Kickback Mode, significantly reducing the weight.

The MCON controller supports any iPhone equipped with MagSafe, as well as any Android phone with a built-in magnetic ring or magnetic case. A magnetic ring is included in the box that you can attach to devices without MagSafe. The MCON is compatible with controller-supported mobile games, Apple Arcade, emulators, Steam Link, PlayStation Remote Play, GeForce Now, and Xbox cloud gaming. Now that we've covered the specs, let me talk about my actual hands-on experience.

My Usage Experience

What impressed me most was, of course, the build quality. The way they've combined magnets, metal, and plastic gives it a wonderfully substantial feel in the hand. Designs with this many moving parts usually have some level of sticking or compromise, but I didn't experience any of that. From the sliding mechanism to removing and reattaching the metal baseplate to switch to Kickback Mode, every action felt smooth. I also really appreciate that it has a physical power switch, which makes pairing with different devices incredibly convenient. After pairing, it automatically reconnects to your most recently used device every time you power it on.

I tested the controller in three main scenarios. First was Xbox cloud gaming. I play a lot of NCAA Football on Xbox, so I wanted to see how NCAA performed on the iPhone using the MCON. The controller easily delivered a console-grade gaming experience in the palm of my hand, which was fantastic. Then I used it to play Madden 27 on Apple Arcade. The game natively supports MFi controllers, so it worked perfectly. Thanks to the zero latency, it actually felt like an even better experience than cloud gaming. Madden 27 is also an excellent choice for players who want a console-quality Madden experience on the go. Finally, I used it for a more casual Game Boy emulator setup. I love revisiting Pokémon games on my iPhone. The emulator I regularly use fully supports external controllers, so that was no problem either.

I played for almost two hours straight, tried it multiple times, and my hands never felt fatigued. I also tried Kickback Mode, which was very comfortable. It's even better with a foldable phone, because you get a massive screen to game on.

The only downside I found is that the controller cannot charge your iPhone, whether via MagSafe or wired charging. Other than that, this controller completely meets my needs.

Pricing and Availability

The Ohsnap MCON controller is currently on sale at the Ohsnap website for $99 (originally $149). It's available in black and white. There's also a solid accessory ecosystem you can pick up, including a carrying case, an accessory similar to a Switch dock that can cast to your TV, and several other notable accessories.

Final Verdict

For me, this controller absolutely did not disappoint. As I mentioned, I saw it in person over a year ago and knew I had to get one. If you're old enough to remember the T-Mobile SideKick, it actually reminds me of that device. The ability to have your phone pop out and instantly become a professional-grade controller, yet still fit in your pocket, is absolutely fantastic. Excellent build quality, a unique yet practical design, and strong game compatibility make it a recommended choice for anyone looking to buy a portable gaming controller. What do you think? Do you play console-like games on your iPhone? Are you currently using a portable controller? Drop a comment and let's discuss!
